record.title: Norway restricts temporary entry of Russian-registered passenger cars, October 2023
record.scope: Norwegian external import regime, explicitly applicable to the Storskog land crossing.
record.crossings: Storskog; no other land crossing is independently located in this round
record.movement: Non-exempt Russian-registered passenger cars with nine or fewer seats, including temporary imports
record.exceptions: Vehicles with ten or more seats remain possible. Specified Norwegian/EEA citizen-owned and qualifying family vehicles are excepted under the notice’s citizenship and permanent-residence conditions; humanitarian, diplomatic, international-organisation and state-courier vehicles also have specified exceptions.
record.enforcement: Official policy and later dated instruction recovered; no particular first vehicle refusal inspected.
record.consequences: No general economic effect is quantified in this round.
record.relationship: EU010 concerns Russian persons arriving for non-essential purposes from May 2024. The October 2023 import rule attaches to a vehicle and leaves personal admission conditions separate.
record.status_observation: Historical source evidence only. Unknown endpoint does not establish the present status of the border.

record.current_corrections: The vehicle rule is distinct from the May 2024 personal-admission policy. Specified exceptions remain; no final lifting or uninterrupted refusal of all cars is established.
record.rationale_coding_status: Source-attributed coding accepted after separate challenge; qualifications retained

followup_reviews.Research finding: Occurrence and inclusion remain supported for the October 2023 vehicle-import rule, separate from EU010 personal admission in May 2024. Retain Russian-registered cars with nine or fewer seats, temporary imports and stated ownership/residence, humanitarian and official-vehicle exceptions. Ten-plus-seat vehicles and individual admission are not universally closed. P1 retains formal-policy onset 3 October 2023 (2 October 24:00), confirmation through 23 May 2024 and the 233-calendar-day lower bound for the rule only. No endpoint or complete operational duration is established. Retain attributed Interstate disputes and pressure / Sanctions and coercive pressure. The minister expressly frames the rule as reducing resources available for Russia’s war. The launch article was freshly read; the later instruction was reread from its preserved PDF text. These are one national-government source family, not independent observation of every refusal. The Storskog phase remains unlocated with null coordinates and dated-evidence-only display. The source names the post but does not supply approved marker geometry.
